knowledge:
- key_parameters: method in getDefaultXcmsSetStartingParams = Specifies the peak picking method, currently supporting 'matchedFilter' or 'centWave' ;; files in optimizeXcmsSet = Character vector of raw data file paths used for peak picking optimization (typically quality control samples) ;; params in optimizeXcmsSet / optimizeRetGroup = A list of starting parameters where ranges (two values) are optimized and single values are kept constant ;; nSlaves = Number of parallel DoE experiments to run ;; subdir = Directory path to save response surface models (RSM), or NULL to disable saving ;; xset in optimizeRetGroup = An xcmsSet object used as the basis for retention time correction and grouping optimization
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: When preprocessing untargeted metabolomics raw data (e.g., in CDF or other xcms-compatible formats) and needing to systematically optimize peak picking, retention time correction, and grouping parameters rather than guessing
- pitfalls: If a parameter should not be optimized, set it to a single default value instead of NULL ;; For the 'centWave' method, the 'peakwidth' parameter must be split into 'min_peakwidth' and 'max_peakwidth' for optimization ;; For the 'centWave' method, the 'prefilter' parameter must be split into 'prefilter' (first value) and 'prefilter_value' (second value) for optimization ;; Only 'obiwarp' (retention time correction) and 'density' (grouping) methods are currently supported for simultaneous retention time and grouping optimization

workflows.name: xcms_parameter_optimization
workflows.intent: Optimize XCMS peak picking, retention time correction, and grouping parameters using Design of Experiments (DoE) and generate an optimized processing script.
input: datafiles (character vector of raw mass spectrometry files, e.g., CDF or mzML format)
workflows.stages: 1. Define starting parameters for peak picking using getDefaultXcmsSetStartingParams and customize ranges ;; 2. Optimize peak picking parameters using optimizeXcmsSet ;; 3. Define starting parameters for retention time correction and grouping using getDefaultRetGroupStartingParams ;; 4. Optimize retention time correction and grouping parameters simultaneously using optimizeRetGroup ;; 5. Generate an optimized R processing script using writeRScript
workflows.code:
datapath <- system.file("cdf", package = "faahKO")
datafiles <- list.files(datapath, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

library(IPO)

peakpickingParameters <- getDefaultXcmsSetStartingParams('matchedFilter')
#setting levels for step to 0.2 and 0.3 (hence 0.25 is the center point)
peakpickingParameters$step <- c(0.2, 0.3)
peakpickingParameters$fwhm <- c(40, 50)
#setting only one value for steps therefore this parameter is not optimized
peakpickingParameters$steps <- 2

time.xcmsSet <- system.time({ # measuring time
resultPeakpicking <- 
  optimizeXcmsSet(files = datafiles[1:2], 
                  params = peakpickingParameters, 
                  nSlaves = 1, 
                  subdir = NULL,
                  plot = TRUE)
})

resultPeakpicking$best_settings$result
optimizedXcmsSetObject <- resultPeakpicking$best_settings$xset

retcorGroupParameters <- getDefaultRetGroupStartingParams()
retcorGroupParameters$profStep <- 1
retcorGroupParameters$gapExtend <- 2.7
time.RetGroup <- system.time({ # measuring time
resultRetcorGroup <-
  optimizeRetGroup(xset = optimizedXcmsSetObject, 
                   params = retcorGroupParameters, 
                   nSlaves = 1, 
                   subdir = NULL,
                   plot = TRUE)
})

writeRScript(resultPeakpicking$best_settings$parameters, 
             resultRetcorGroup$best_settings)
